S17 PREP (researcher-10, 2026-05-16) — PREP that ships PASTE-READY recipes derived from a predecessor STATE-SYNC's `nextAction` sketch must ROUND-TRIP the sketch's named symbols against the actual file API. Here the S16 STATE-SYNC §5.1 named `DiscreteMemorylessChannel` and `InputDistribution` (which do NOT exist; actual names `DMChannel` line 34 + `InputDist` line 40) and dot-notation methods `ch.channelMI` / `ch.channelCapacity` (which are NOT methods — `channelMI ch inp` / `channelCapacity ch`). A blind S17 ACT against the S16 recipe would have failed at the very first `theorem` line. The PREP's primary defensive value is precisely THIS kind of round-trip — beyond the bearer drift recheck of *existing* symbols, audit that *referenced* symbols actually exist in the current API surface.

S17 PREP (researcher-10, 2026-05-16) — The S16 STATE-SYNC §5.1 named S17-medium with the converse-direction statement `capacity-achieving + symmetric ⇒ uniform input`. This is FALSE in general — BSC(p=1/2) has `W true · ↦ ⟨1/2,1/2⟩` = `W false · ↦ ⟨1/2,1/2⟩`, hence `channelMI ch inp = 0` for ALL inputs, so capacity = 0 and EVERY input trivially achieves it. The standard textbook result is the FORWARD direction only: `uniform input ACHIEVES capacity for weakly symmetric channels`. Uniqueness of the capacity-achieving input requires strict concavity arguments excluding degeneracy — beyond S18's scope. Lesson: when a STATE-SYNC names an aspirational theorem statement WITHOUT first proving forward + backward directions are individually correct, the PREP must split into forward vs converse and check each against literature.

S17 PREP (researcher-10, 2026-05-16) — Cover-Thomas §7.2 distinguishes `symmetric` (rows are permutations of each other AND columns are permutations of each other) from `weakly symmetric` (rows are permutations AND each column sums to the same constant). For the result `uniform input achieves capacity`, WEAKLY symmetric is sufficient and is the right tradeoff. The full `symmetric` predicate is strictly stronger (column-permutation ⇒ column-sum-constancy, but not conversely) and harder to verify in practice (needs explicit α-permutation rather than arithmetic equality of sums). Recommendation: define `IsWeaklySymmetric` only; defer `IsSymmetric` (the stronger variant) for future need.

S8 (2026-05-12): The maximum-entropy equality case `H(p) = log|α| ↔ p ≡ uniform` factors cleanly through the KL-equality case `klDivergence p q = 0 ↔ p ≡ q`. The connecting identity `KL(p||uniform) + H(p) = log|α|` follows term-by-term from `log(p/((card α)⁻¹)) = log(p) + log(card α)`, so the iff reduces to KL vanishing. The strict log inequality `0 < y → y ≠ 1 → log y < y - 1` is derived from `Real.add_one_lt_exp` (which requires `x ≠ 0`) by setting `x = log y` and using `Real.exp_log hy = y`.

S7 (2026-05-12): The Shannon-form converse `(1 - P_e) · log |α| ≤ C + h(P_e)` is a one-step nlinarith-closed rearrangement of the Fano-form `log |α| ≤ C + h(P_e) + P_e · log(|α| - 1)` — the slack `P_e · log(|α| - 1) ≤ P_e · log |α|` is absorbed via `Real.log_le_log` on `|α| - 1 ≤ |α|`, valid for `|α| ≥ 2`. The Shannon-form is the cleaner downstream API: it factors `(1 - P_e)` as a multiplier of `log |α|`, isolating the rate-vs-capacity gap on one side.
The two conditionalEntropy definitions are body-identical, hence rfl-equal; this lets the bridge use a term-mode `:=` instead of a tactic rewrite.
For |α|=1, both sides of Fano simplify to 0: H(X|Y)=0 (degenerate ratio inside log), P_e=0 (singleton collapse), and (card α : ℝ) - 1 = 0 annihilates the second RHS term.
Empty α is vacuous via Finset.univ_eq_empty + sum_empty contradicting hsum=1.
fano_inequality_proved signature matches axiom byte-for-byte modulo the `(Fintype.card α : ℝ)` cast (both files use the same cast form).

Term-mode reference `:= dispatcher pXY hp hsum` suffices for axiom->theorem swap when the dispatcher's body is defeq to the axiom's stated type (unused `let pX` in the axiom unfolds away; Real.log argument elaborates uniformly under expected type ℝ).
